messages:
Alex (PM): heads up — we've got 3 customer asks this week asking for stronger tenant controls on the API surface. they want per-project keys, scoped function calls, and predictable key rotation behavior. can we sketch impact + rollout constraints?

Maria (Eng): quick note: chat/completions vs embeddings vs rerank have different performance/caching shapes. per-project keys mean we need routing metadata on every request header to pick caches and model variants. small perf hit but manageable.

Sam (Sec): +1 on routing metadata. we also need to define what 'scoped' means: read-only embeddings vs full tool-calling? should be policy-driven. also need to think about key rotation expiry windows and session continuity.

Li (Platform): technical constraints: current load-balancer and cache shard uses org_id for affinity. adding project_id is straightforward in the header (e.g., `X-Redwood-Project`) but will increase cardinality of caches and routing table size. estimate: +15% memory for hot caches.

Kai (DevEx): customers ask for minimal friction. prefer API keys that can be created via Console + CLI. rotation UX: create new key, mark old key as 'grace' for N days, auto-expire. docs need code snippets for serverless refresh flows.

Emma (Legal): flag on data residency and audit trails. per-project keys must surface audit logs clearly (who created/rotated keys, which project used them). retention policy TBD but customers in regulated sectors will ask.

Maria (Eng): implementation notes: for function/tool calling we already embed caller metadata into tool invocation RPCs. we need to attach `project_id` -> enforce tool allowlist per project. that will be an access check on the runtime path, small latency add (<1ms) but increases auth checks per token.

Sam (Sec): rotation edge-case: long-running streaming calls — if key rotates mid-stream do we continue the stream? recommended: allow current stream to finish but reject new requests with rotated key. need to design TTL and revocation hooks.

Alex (PM): OK good. propose PRD outline: 1) API model: org vs project keys, 2) scoped capabilities (embeddings read-only, rerank limited, tool-calls gated), 3) key lifecycle and rotation UX + grace period, 4) observability & audit. please call out launch criteria.

Li (Platform): launch criteria (ops): routing supports project_id with 99.9% routing correctness under load, cache mem increase acceptable (<25% cap), no single-shard hotspots.

Maria (Eng): launch criteria (eng): automated tests for per-project deny/allow rules, perf regression <5% P95 on chat endpoints, tool-call allowlist enforcement end-to-end.

Sam (Sec): launch criteria (sec): key revocation takes effect within X seconds in typical case, documented revocation and rotation flows, threat model updated.

Emma (Legal): launch criteria (legal/compliance): audit log entries for key create/rotate/revoke available in Console and via API, retention configurable for enterprise customers.

Kai (DevEx): launch criteria (DX): Console + CLI flows for key create/rotate/revoke, sample code for silent rotation (server-to-server), one migration guide for org->project split.

Alex (PM): prioritization ask: do we 1) land project-scoped keys first, 2) land capability scoping, or 3) land rotation UX? customers want rotation + scoping together but we could stage. thoughts?

Maria (Eng): tech prefers project keys first (low-level routing + cache changes) so capability scoping builds on top. rotation UX can be parallel but needs the graceful revocation hooks implemented in platform.

Sam (Sec): security priority: rotation and revocation must be in the first release (even if UX is minimal), otherwise customers won't trust scoped keys. suggest short grace period + manual revoke API in alpha.

Li (Platform): rollout plan: beta with opt-in per org, telemetry enabled to measure cache/memory impact. 2-week canary in a dedicated cluster, then open beta.

Kai (DevEx): docs plan: beta guide, quickstart, and migration sample. also add code snippet for rotation header example:```
# refresh flow (server)
new_key = POST /v1/keys
old_key -> mark grace
client rotates to new_key within 24h
```

Alex (PM): action items: Maria to draft API spec for headers + project-scoped keys by EOW; Sam to write rotation threat model & recommend default grace window; Li to prototype routing change and report mem delta; Kai to draft docs skeleton; Emma to note compliance asks. sync Fri 10am.

infra-bot: Deployment window scheduled: fri-10am -> feature-flag toggle available for beta orgs.

Sam (Sec): one more: for function calling, recommend adding `allowed_tools` claim on the key metadata so that server can enforce without extra DB lookups. store in cache with TTL.

Maria (Eng): yep that aligns — we can put `allowed_tools` in the key resource and cache it; invalidation on rotate/revoke.

Alex (PM): perfect — this gives me enough to write a prioritized roadmap entry. thanks all. :tada:
